To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in vivo, ethanol inhibits the potentiated upregulation of nitric oxide synthetase by lipopolysac-charide and autacoids, but not by autacoids alone.
in vivo, ETOH selectively suppressed LPS-induced, but not autacoid-induced, upregulation of rat AMs iNOS mRNA and protein and RNIs.

ethanol and the antioxidant diethyldithiocarbamate inhibit endotoxin-induced upregulation and expression of the inducible nitrite oxide synthase in the rat lung alveolar macrophone by a mechanism that involves the nuclear transcription factor kappa B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the autacoids in the regulation of the iN0S pathway.
elucidating mechanisms that may be involved in the pathogenesis of acute alcohol-induced lung injury.
the effect of EOH on LPS-induced up-regulation of iN0S.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ETOH inhibiting iNOS expression in AMs is due to its ability to block the LPS-induced activation of the NF-kappa B pathway.
ETOH inhibiting the upregulation of LPS-stimulating iNOS mRNA by autacoid-stimulating i NOS mRNA is a mechanism independent of the NF-kappa pathway.
ETOH suppresses the potentiation of LPS by autacoids in vivo by a mechanism that involves inhibition of NF-kappaB and inhibition of translation of iNOS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ETOH selectively suppresses the potentiation of LPS-induced iNOS upregulation by autacoids in rat lung macrophages.
ETOH selectively inhibits iNOS protein formation in AMs stimulated by LPS in vivo.
ethanol inhibits the upregulation of endotoxin-stimulated iNOS in rat alveolarmacrophages in vivo, but not in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ETOH inhibitory effects on the LPS-induced up-regulation of iN OS mRNA, protein, RNI, TNF-alpha mRNA, and cell-associated TNF-alpha protein are independent of its ability either to suppress NF-kappa B or to inhibit iNOS transcription.
ETOH inhibited LPS-stimulating, but not db-cAMP- or 2-methylothio-ATP-stimulated, upregulation of AM iNOS in vivo.
ETOH can selectively suppress the upregulation of inflammatory genes in AMs in vivo by inhibiting LPS-induced NF-kappaB activation, but does not affect autacoid-induced upregulation.
